traceability.notes: Performance data extracted by claude-sonnet-5 reading the PDF directly (native document input), used as a fallback because the deterministic pdfplumber pipeline (summary_report_parser.py) found no per-category breakdown in this report. Model's own extraction notes: This report covers a qualitative (detection) method (NEOGEN Molecular Detection Assay 2 - Listeria monocytogenes) validated under EN ISO 16140-2:2016, with an initial validation (2016, General Protocol + Specific Protocol 1) covering 6 categories, and a later 2024 extension study (Specific Protocol 2) covering 3 additional category variants (Meat products, Dairy products, Seafood/fishery products - extension) tested with a new enrichment broth (LESS Plus). I recorded the 6 primary/canonical categories from Table 6 (General Protocol + Specific Protocol 1, the original validation scope covering the full breadth of food categories: Composite foods, Meat products, Dairy products, Vegetables, Seafood and fishery products, Environmental samples). The extension-study results (SP2: Meat products, Dairy/Milk products, Seafood and fishery products) are separate re-tests of already-covered categories under a different enrichment protocol, so per the instructions I excluded them as they duplicate categories already listed under the primary study; their summary sensitivity/trueness/FPR values were: Meat products (SP2 ext) SEalt=81.3%, SEref=84.4%, RT=84.5%, FPR=0.0%; Milk and Dairy products (SP2 ext) SEalt=90.6%, SEref=96.9%, RT=93.5%, FPR=0.0%; Seafood and fishery products (SP2 ext) SEalt=86.8%, SEref=89.5%, RT=87.8%, FPR=0.0%. Also excluded aggregate/total rows ("All categories and all protocols", "General protocol + specific protocol 1", "General protocol + specific protocol 2"). Certificate number taken from cover page title "(certificate # 3M 01/15 – 09/16)".
